description: CommandRegistry.serializer_codec_for(order_type) resolves first-match when multiple specs share an OrderType, making it advisory rather than authoritative. Today no production specs share an OrderType so the lookup is unambiguous; the new ratchet test_specs_sharing_order_type_declare_same_codec (added in PROJ-438 Phase 9) fires the moment a future change introduces an OrderType-sharing spec pair with inconsistent codecs. def has_cargo_resources(self, costs: Dict[str, float]) -> bool:
        """Check if fleet cargo contains all required resources.
description: Fleet production has an affordability-vs-consumption rounding mismatch that PROJ-436 Phase 12 (Option C) intentionally left in place. Fleet.has_cargo_resources (fleet.py:245) compares against the unrounded float request, while Fleet.consume_cargo_resource (fleet.py:262) does int(round(amount)) before unloading from the integer-typed cargo store. Result for fractional per-step fleet costs that round to 0 (e.g. requested 0.1 against cargo=1): affordability PASSES, the engine consumes (actually 0 charged), ProductionEngine._apply_resource_consumption records 0 progress via Phase 12's diff truth-up, _process_queue_tick_dynamic decrements tick_capacity, and the queue stalls correctly without progressing — but does NOT emit a RESOURCE_SHORTAGE event because the affordability check passed. UX gap: the player sees a stuck fleet build with no shortage indicator. Latent in current data/components.json (ratios produce integer per-step costs); becomes visible as soon as a new ship class lands fractional ratios on fleet builds.
suggested_action: Two options. (a) In ProductionEngine._apply_resource_consumption, detect 'amount > 0 was requested but actually_consumed == 0' (the diff is zero) and route to _log_resource_shortage with the rounding-vs-cargo cause. (b) Change Fleet.has_cargo_resources to compare against int(round(amount)) so affordability matches consumption semantics. Either path is small; (a) is more honest about the actual state, (b) is symmetric with the consume side. PROJ-436 Phase 12 Codex consult artifact at AgentCoordination/Scratchpad/Consult/20260518T154523Z_proj436-phase12-fractional-fleet-cost/response.md (Risk #1) is the source.
resolution_note: PROJ-444 Phase 2 (2026-05-18) applied Option B at the data-layer: Fleet.has_cargo_resources now compares against int(round(amount)), symmetric with consume_cargo_resource's rounding. Both sides agree on what gets charged. The remaining UX gap — no RESOURCE_SHORTAGE emitted when amount rounds to 0 — is the engine-side Option A path (ProductionEngine._apply_resource_consumption) and remains open; it belongs to PROJ-445 territory.

code_snippet:
def _apply_resource_consumption(
        self,
description: Forward-contract risk in ProductionEngine._apply_resource_consumption: the method ignores the bool return of production_consume_resource and only records the production_get_resource before/after diff (Phase 12 Option C truth-up). If a future IProductionResourceSource implementation returns False from production_consume_resource AFTER the affordability check passed — e.g. a sub-tick race condition between affordability and consume, or a partial-charge contract — the diff records 0 progress but _process_queue_tick_dynamic still subtracts ticks_to_spend from tick_capacity. Result: tick capacity burns without forward progress. No present production caller exercises this (Planet and Fleet both currently succeed when affordability passes), but the IProductionResourceSource Protocol contract permits the failure mode. The Phase 12 Protocol docstring update implies but does not enforce 'consume MUST succeed when affordability passed'.
suggested_action: Two options. (a) Capture the consume return value in _apply_resource_consumption and signal back to _process_queue_tick_dynamic so it can skip the tick_capacity decrement when consume returned False (preserves capacity for a retry or shortage). (b) Tighten the IProductionResourceSource Protocol contract to explicitly declare 'production_consume_resource MUST succeed when affordability passed' so failure is a programmer error rather than a contract-permitted outcome. (b) is cheaper; (a) is more defensive against future implementers. Codex Phase 12 consult artifact at AgentCoordination/Scratchpad/Consult/20260518T154523Z_proj436-phase12-fractional-fleet-cost/response.md (Risk #2) is the source.
